title: Reacher Grabber Tools: Pick Things Up Without Bending, and How to Choose One
subtitle: A simple, inexpensive tool can save some stooping and stretching, as long as you pick the right claw and know its limits.
excerpt: A reacher grabber can help you pick up a dropped pill bottle or a light item without bending down. Here is what these tools do, what to look for, and three Vive Health models to consider.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: It happens a dozen times a day. A sock slips off the bed, the TV remote rolls under the couch, or a light item lands on the floor just out of reach. For many of us, bending down or stretching up is no longer as easy as it once was, and every awkward stoop can leave us off balance.

A reacher, sometimes called a grabber or pick-up tool, is one of the simplest helpers you can keep around the house. It is a lightweight pole with a handle at one end and a claw at the other. You squeeze the trigger, and the claw closes on what you are after. No batteries, no apps and no monthly fees.

The three models below are all from one maker, Vive Health, and each is listed with a 32-inch reach. That makes them easy to compare with each other, but it is a narrow view. We have not researched other brands in this article, so treat it as a starting point rather than a full market survey.

The differences are in the details. A rotating claw turns so the jaws can grip at different angles, which the research notes say helps with dressing. A folding reacher has a hinge in the middle, so it can be stored in a smaller space. Suction-cup tips are rubber pads meant for smooth items such as glasses, electronics and bulbs.

It helps to be clear about what a reacher cannot do. It is not a medical alert device and will not call for help. It will not help someone get up after a fall. It also carries only light loads: Vive lists up to about 5 pounds for its rotating model. Do not use one to lift heavy items or to pull on rugs or drawers. And it does not replace standing up or sitting down safely.

items: Grip strength: every trigger takes some squeezing. If arthritis or weak hands make that painful, look at models built for a lighter grip before you buy.
Claw style: suction tips suit smooth things only, not rough or textured ones.
Rotating head: may help if you want assistance with dressing.
Folding or fixed: a folding model may be easier to tuck away; check the maker's page for how it folds.
Weight limit: check the listed load, and keep to small, light items.

Price and warranty: Vive's own pages disagree on the rotating model's warranty (lifetime on one, 1 year on another), and prices differ between its site, its collection page and dealers. Confirm both on the live product page.
Returns: we did not check shipping or return policies, so look at the seller's terms. How a handle feels in your hand is hard to judge online.

sections.content: Consider keeping a reacher where you tend to drop things, such as by the bed or a favorite chair. If you have more than one, a second spot near where you dress or sit may save you some walking.

As general common-sense tips, try it first on soft, unbreakable items like a sock until you get a feel for how hard to squeeze. If you can, pick things up close to you rather than far out in front. Keep heavy or breakable items on lower shelves, within easy reach and well under the weight limit.

Hand strength matters. The Consumers Guide, a review site that ranks products in a best-of list rather than an independent testing body, picked Vive as best for most people. For arthritis or a weak grip it pointed to a different tool, the Carex Ultra Grabber, calling it "the one to buy if arthritis or hand weakness makes holding a squeeze painful" (The Consumers Guide, Best Reacher Grabbers for Seniors, 2026). We have not researched the Carex, so check its details yourself.

A reacher can cut down on some bending and stretching, but it does not replace other safety steps. This is general advice, not from a specific source: if you have trouble standing, have fallen recently or are recovering from surgery, ask your doctor what is right for you. In an emergency, call 911.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: A reacher is a small purchase, so it is worth choosing with care. Pick a claw that suits the things you grab most, check that the handle is comfortable for your hands, and confirm the price and warranty on the live page before you order.

products.name: Vive Rotating Reacher Grabber, 32"
products.blurb: Suits people who want help with dressing. Listed with a 4-inch-wide claw that rotates 90 degrees, a contoured trigger handle, and a hold of up to about 5 pounds per Vive. Warranty is listed inconsistently, so confirm it.

products.name: Vive Folding Reacher Grabber, 32"
products.blurb: May suit anyone who wants a reacher that folds for storage. The maker's page lists a 32-inch reach and a rotating head; a fold-down size, push-button hinge and rubber lining appear in other listing copy, so confirm them on the maker's page.

products.name: Vive Folding Suction Cup Reacher, 32"
products.blurb: Aimed at smooth items such as glasses, electronics and bulbs. It has a pull trigger, rubber suction tips and a hinge that folds the pole in half. Those details come from the maker's own copy, which is not independent, so confirm them.
